# ABISS: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Systems Through Agent Interaction

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#abiss)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.23340v1) · arXiv:2607.23340v1, 25 July 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 17 PDF pages: Sections 1-7.1, Appendices A-D, Tables 1-10, figure captions and references; Figure 2 and Tables 4-6 visually checked.

## Research question

Separate problematic-question diagnosis from clarification-conditioned SQL generation and explanations of unsupported requests.

## Method

Defines eight problem categories, generates paired interpretations or unsupported cases, filters them with a three-model council, and simulates style-conditioned dialogue. Ambiguity filtering removes dominant readings; unanswerability means no council-generated valid SQL was found.

## Evaluation

Eight models, four category-information modes, balanced BIRD/Spider subsets, three clarification turns plus a final response. Execution matching tolerates extra columns; feedback is council-judged. Human audits cover 52 questions and 150 conversations, not the whole dataset.

## What the results support

Oracle categories improve ambiguous execution and refusal feedback, but final SQL remains difficult. Termination after relevant feedback can be high while execution accuracy stays low.

## Limits and qualifications

Council membership overlaps generation, evaluation and tested models. The small human audit reports 75% SQL correctness. Simulated users do not give vague or incorrect clarifications or change intent. For benchmark-unanswerable items, the user simulator refuses clarification requests; this is not a guarantee that the evaluated SQL agent refuses.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A controlled diagnostic benchmark, not proof of unanswerability or evidence of real-user dialogue reliability.
